input.summary:
parts/room-18.mjs (P2 kitchen) now places no blocks: its 10 furniture writes were all refused because the shell already owns the kitchen's interior air (y2..4).
I removed them, so ./make.sh shows "room: P2 kitchen: 0 placed" with no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE, and build.nbt was saved (5948 cells).
The real problem is in shell-west.mjs house(), which carves every interior as air and locks it, so all 55 room parts place 0 blocks, not only this one; I did not edit that module.
left: The P2 kitchen is unfurnished. I removed the stove run (barrel, smoker, furnace, cauldron), the table (fence post and top slab), the stair chair, the pantry barrel, the potted poppy and the lantern. The header comment still describes the intended furniture.

Root cause, outside this part: shell-west.mjs house() fills each plot's interior with air at y2..top, and runParts marks every cell an earlier part wrote (air included) as owned. Every room part therefore places 0 blocks (all 55 rooms in the make.sh output), not just room-18. The fix belongs in the shell module: leave interior cells unwritten, or let room parts own their own air.
No OFF-PALETTE blocks were reported for this part, so no palette swaps were needed.

waste.what: Worked out why the writes were refused by reading runParts in build.mjs (the owned set, and that air counts as owned), since the REFUSED line only says 'had: air' with no owner.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls, reading roughly 60 lines of build.mjs
waste.tool: runParts' REFUSED line should name the earlier part that owns the cell (for example 'owned by shell west (plots 0-3) house()'), so the cause is visible at once.

waste.what: Counted the refused writes by hand: the report shows refusedAt.slice(0, 8) while the count is 10, so the last two (the potted poppy and the lantern) had to be found by reading the layers.
waste.cost: one extra reading pass over room-18.mjs
waste.tool: Print every refused cell, or the total with the full list in parts-report.json, instead of truncating at 8.

waste.what: Had no way to ask which cells in a box are still free before writing; the only way to learn that the kitchen was locked was to run the whole build.
waste.cost: one full make.sh run per probe (about 5948 cells rebuilt each time)
waste.tool: A command such as `mcd free build.nbt --box 39,2,19,43,4,20` (or a runParts dry-run flag) listing cells that no earlier part owns, so a designer can plan a room before writing.

companions.task: Own the shell's house() interior: stop carving the room cells as air so the room designers can place furniture into them. Also check the other shell parts for the same pattern.
Once the kitchen interior is free, hang the lantern from the y5 ceiling block (or stand it on the table) so the kitchen is not dark.
